readout.purpose: The big numbers on their tiles — countdown, interval phase, clock, laps. IBM Plex Sans Condensed 600, tabular figures.

readout-display.purpose: The fullscreen display's giant readout, clamp(3rem, 16vmin, 7rem); the wall clock goes to clamp(4rem, 22vmin, 10rem).

label.purpose: Buttons, nav links, taglines, phase chips — 14px 600 uppercase, wide tracking, carried by CSS text-transform.

body.purpose: Descriptions, forms, settings — IBM Plex Sans for everything said.

motion.name: flap-turn
motion.purpose: The one authored motion: the digit that changes flips — a half-turn through 90°, quantized in six frames like a motor stepping through its cams. Only remounted tiles play it. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: state-color
motion.purpose: Quiet color-only transitions on interactive elements — the only other motion in the app.

breakpoints.name: single-column
breakpoints.note: Tool pages are one centered max-w-3xl column at every width; the top bar scrolls horizontally; the display sizes by vmin.

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.note: Readouts step up one size class (e.g. text-6xl → text-8xl on the stopwatch).

components.name: Flip Readout
components.description: The signature readout: each digit on its own bone tile with the hinge seam; only a changed digit flips.
components.html: 10:00
components.css: .ds-flip-row { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 0.09em; font-size: 48px; } .ds-flap { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; width: 0.84em; height: 1.3em; background: var(--tile, #ece5d3); color: var(--tile-ink, #1d231f); border-radius: 2px; position: relative; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed', 'Avenir Next Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-flap::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; top: 50%; height: 1px; background: var(--seam, rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.22)); } .ds-flip-sep { font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed', 'Avenir Next Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1; color: var(--ink, #ede7d9); } @keyframes ds-flap-turn { 0% { transform: perspective(0.6em) rotateX(0deg); filter: brightness(1); } 50% { transform: perspective(0.6em) rotateX(-90deg); filter: brightness(0.55); } 100% { transform: perspective(0.6em) rotateX(0deg); filter: brightness(1); } } .ds-flap-turn { animation: ds-flap-turn 260ms steps(6, end) both; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-flap-turn { animation: none; } }

narrative.overview:
tick descends from the split-flap departure board: rows of tiles that flip to their next truth, read from across a station hall by people who cannot stop walking. The interface is that board turned inward — time as printed matter. Slate-green ground, bone tiles, a condensed grotesque for everything measured, and exactly one vermilion signal for whatever is "now". It refuses the two neighboring defaults: the gradient-ring focus app and the white minimalist clock clone. There is no glass, no glow, no gradient, no circle; the board carries the design, and the vermilion says "now".

The app opens straight on the countdowns — there is no home, no landing pitch. A slim persistent bar carries the wordmark and the eight tools; every page is one centered column of working controls; the fullscreen display is one number as large as the viewport allows. Progress is never a bar or a ring: it is a row of small tiles filling with vermilion, the board spending itself.
keyCharacteristics: Slate ground, bone tiles, one vermilion signal — vermilion appears only on what runs, what is done, or what is focused, never as decoration.
Tiles are the unit: digits live on tiles, progress is a row of tiles, the metronome's beats are tiles.
The condensed grotesque (IBM Plex Sans Condensed) for everything measured or labelled; IBM Plex Sans for everything said.
Flat: depth comes from tonal steps (bg → surface → surface-2) and 1px lines, never shadows.
One authored motion: the mechanical flip of the digit that changes; nothing else in the app moves.

rules.name: The Signal Tile Rule
rules.body: Vermilion marks exactly one thing per glance: what runs, is done, or is focused. If a second element wants vermilion, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Inverted Material Rule
rules.body: The light theme is the same board with its material inverted — paper ground, slate tiles — not a second palette. Roles never change sides between themes.

rules.name: The Digits Don't Dance Rule
rules.body: Every digit sits on its own tile: the tile fixes the column, not just tnum. A readout too small for tiles (an input, a table cell) still uses the condensed face with tabular figures via .tnum. A running digit column that shifts is a defect, at any size.

rules.name: The Flat Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, ever. If a surface needs to feel raised, give it surface over bg and a line border — or it does not need to feel raised.

rules.name: The One Motion Rule
rules.body: The flap flip (flap-turn, 260ms, steps(6, end) — a half-turn through 90°, quantized like a motor stepping through its cams) is the only animation in the app. Everything else changes by state-color transition. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce turns the flip into an instant change; no motion is ever load-bearing.

dos: Do use vermilion for running, done, and focused — and nothing else (The Signal Tile Rule).
Do put every running digit on a tile, or at minimum in .tnum (The Digits Don't Dance Rule).
Do express progress as a TileRow — tiles filling with vermilion.
Do pull every color, font, and radius from src/components/tokens.css; the browser chrome (selection, caret, scrollbar, title bar) takes the same tokens.
Do size display readouts by vmin/clamp, so the number owns the viewport.
donts: Don't add shadows, gradients, glass, or glow (The Flat Rule).
Don't introduce a second accent color, a cool/gray neutral, or a pure white.
Don't add a progress bar, an arc, a ring, or a dial — or any circle at all — where a TileRow belongs.
Don't animate anything beyond the flap flip and state-color transitions (The One Motion Rule).
Don't use a proportional (non-tabular) figure in a running readout, or a mono face: the condensed grotesque is the voice.
Don't load a font or asset from a network origin — assets are self-hosted, and the privacy gate fails the build otherwise.
